page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-c32g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. It features 188.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 5.88 GB per vCPU, alongside a 48 MB Level 3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI instructions. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPU with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance includes a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and contains no local storage, requiring external cloud disks for persistent filesystem requirements.

Benchmark measurements place the host CPU and memory subsystem in the middle 50 percent across standard metrics, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 13808.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 36547.02. Memory throughput reaches 126.91 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 53.4 GB/sec for uncached writes. In contrast to the baseline CPU scores, accelerator performance is notable in language model execution. The system achieves top-tier results in small and medium large language model inference, processing 9700.0 prompt tokens per second and 454.43 generation tokens per second on a 135M model, alongside 2489.49 prompt tokens per second and 90.21 generation tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the pairing of a single enterprise A10 GPU with a substantial 188.0 GB host memory pool provides an economical configuration for inference workloads compared to multi-GPU deployments. This resource ratio prevents excessive overprovisioning of compute capacity when handling moderate parameter models. The absence of local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, as I/O-intensive pipelines must account for network storage latency, and the 24 GB VRAM ceiling restricts standalone execution of 70B parameter models without quantization or model parallelism.

This server type is suited for transformer model inference, computer vision pipelines, video transcoding, visual computing, and graphics rendering. It also accommodates parallelized data preprocessing workflows that feed directly into GPU-accelerated algorithms.

It operates on x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor and provides 16 Gbps baseline network throughput. Standard compute and memory benchmarks place the host CPU in the average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 36547.02. However, the system demonstrates top-tier efficiency in AI inference benchmarks, processing 2489.49 prompt tokens per second on 7B models. The server lacks bundled local storage, necessitating network-attached disks for persistent data. This hardware profile provides a cost-effective platform for production deep learning inference, image and video processing, and graphics workloads.
